item.title: Fix off-by-one in sliding_windows (window.py)
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): in this repository `python3 -m unittest` fails. Find and fix the bug in `window.py` so every test passes, without changing the tests, and make sure the function is correct for every input, not just the tested ones. Commit the fix.

Known cause: `sliding_windows` returns `range(len(items) - size)`, which drops the last window. The range must be `range(len(items) - size + 1)`. Verify the edge cases by reading the code: when size > len(items) the result must be an empty list, when items is empty with size 1 or more the result must be an empty list, and size 1 must give one window per item. Keep the existing ValueError for size <= 0. Do not modify test_window.py or any test. Keep the change minimal, with no new abstractions. Run `python3 -m unittest` and confirm every test passes before committing. Commit as the repository's configured git user only, with no tool attribution in the commit message.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

pr.body: Approach: change the range end in sliding_windows from len(items) - size to len(items) - size + 1. Key file: window.py (one line). Checks: python3 -m unittest, 3 tests OK after fix (2 failures before). Edge cases verified by reading and by assertions: size > len gives [], empty items gives [] for size >= 1, size 1 gives one window per item, size <= 0 still raises ValueError. Assumptions: size is a positive int, as the existing ValueError guard implies. Tests unchanged.
pr.summary: made sliding_windows return every window again. now includes the final window. before: range(len-size) dropped last window, now: range(len-size+1).
